verdict.rationale: Porkbun documents DNS hosting on its own nameservers with full CRUD across a broad set of record types: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SRV, CAA, TLSA, SSHFP, ALIAS, HTTPS and SVCB, plus DNSSEC DS records. One community user praises the minimalist, fast-loading UI, while another calls it barebones; that is a matter of opinion, not a concrete contradiction. missing for 10: any evidence on minimum or low TTL support, explicit documentation that DNS hosting is free and included with the domain, and first-party documentation of the DNS management UI itself.

support.subject: As a developer, full DNS hosting comes with the domain — every record type, low TTLs, and a management UI that doesn't fight me

citations.quote: Create, read, update, and delete DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SRV, CAA, TLSA, SSHFP, ALIAS, HTTPS, SVCB)
Full CRUD over records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, SRV, CAA, ALIAS, …) and DNSSEC DS records on Porkbun's nameservers
the minimalist UI that actually loads fast was a breath of fresh air and was so much less frustrating than Namecheap
